agree.reason: The lost hospital bids, the partners also coming in three days, and the plain admission that this changes the remote hires' terms will persuade many readers, but a remote hire who stays mainly for remote work gets only $150 and a vague review, so the resisting reader may still push back or leave.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief, but 'working remotely has meant much less of that' treats remote work as the proven cause, and the September 1 start date for the commuting subsidy appears nowhere in the facts given.

works_the_facts.reason: The 30% figure is never turned into something concrete, such as months of lost growth, and two useful facts go unused: 5 of 6 project leads already come in three days, and 15 of 46 means about a third of staff were hired remote.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is shown fairly through the lost bids and slower junior development, but there is no trend and no sense of what keeps happening if nothing changes.

qualification.reason: The six-month review has no date (around March 2028), no measure of success, and no consequence, so the reader cannot hold the firm to it.

objections.reason: The broken hiring terms and commuting costs are addressed, but 'why three days and not fewer?' is not, and readers will ask whether there are desks for everyone, a question the August desk delivery already answers but the email leaves out.

fit.reason: It is a one-page email set before the meeting as asked, but it leaves out the meeting's time and place (10 a.m., main studio).
